text:
maya (infra): seeing a 30% drop in GPU allocatable across us-west-2 cluster, scheduler failing pods with NoDevicePluginAvailable. started after last night's kernel + cuda driver roll
ops-bot: [ALERT] gpu-capacity-drop: us-west-2 (nodes: g3,g4) — 29% allocatable GPUs down :warning:
maya (infra): looks like device-plugin isn't registering on nodes where kernel was bumped. node reports `nvidia driver mismatch` in kubelet events
lee (eng-infra): can you paste the device-plugin logs from a failing node? suspecting the new gpu-operator/device-plugin release we rolled earlier
maya (infra): log snippet from /var/log/containers/nvidia-device-plugin-xxxxx.log:
```
E0418 03:12:14.123 1 deviceplugin.go:182] failed to register with Kubelet: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to discover devices: ioctl(NVML) call failed: NVML_ERROR_LIBRARY_NOT_FOUND
```
maya (infra): `nvidia-smi` also failing on affected hosts: "libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file"
samir (sre): that sounds like driver libs not found — probably driver installed under `/usr/lib/nvidia-525` but symlink `/usr/lib/nvidia` removed after kernel modules rebuilt
jin (platform): i saw a kernel packaging change that switched module path names. device-plugin/version 1.6.0 changed probing to use `/usr/lib/nvidia` hardcoded path. mismatch on nodes that have `nvidia-525` folder ends up failing
lee (eng-infra): hmm the operator rollout included device-plugin 1.6.0 — we have a partial roll where some nodes still run 1.5.x. mixed client behaviour + kernel path change = registration race
maya (infra): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) pause gpu-operator rollout 2) cordon affected nodes and restart gpu-operator DaemonSet there 3) quick symlink fix on nodes (temporary) to point `/usr/lib/nvidia -> /usr/lib/nvidia-525`
samir (sre): agree. also add a node taint so new GPU workloads don't land while we fix. we should avoid mass drains to prevent cross-region failover costs.
kai (oncall): i'll taint and cordon the worst-hit nodes now. patch script to run symlink fix in parallel? will need sudo access on nodes, recommend running via our fleet-ssh job.
lee (eng-infra): commands for fix (testing on one node first):
```
# on node
sudo ln -sfn /usr/lib/nvidia-525 /usr/lib/nvidia
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-docker || true
kubectl -n gpu-operator delete pod -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --force --grace-period=0
# verify
kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[?(@.metadata.name=="NODE_NAME")].status.allocatable}'
nvidia-smi
```
```
# check kubelet events
kubectl describe node NODE_NAME | grep -A3 "device plugin"
```
maya (infra): tried symlink on one node — device-plugin registered, allocatable returned, workloads resumed. good signal
jin (platform): put immediate hold on operator release in CI and roll back device-plugin tag to 1.5.3 for now. i'll open a release freeze PR and patch our helm values to pin version
lee (eng-infra): long term we need to avoid hardcoded driver paths in device-plugin; open an issue to detect both `nvidia` and `nvidia-*` directories and fallback. also add healthcheck gating in rollout
samir (sre): also add a preflight that verifies `nvidia-smi` on nodes after kernel/drivers change before marking node ready for scheduling GPUs. we can reuse the node-problem-detector to make this automatic
maya (infra): cost/regional note: if we had drained pods, they'd have spilled into other regions' spare capacity and we'd hit high on-demand GPU prices and egress charges. avoiding full drains saved ~$7k/day on projected workloads — flagging finance for visibility
lee (eng-infra): action items:
- jin: freeze operator rollout + rollback device-plugin to 1.5.3 (in progress)
- kai: cordon + taint affected nodes (in progress)
- maya: run symlink fix automation for the fleet subset and validate (assigned)
- samir: add preflight healthcheck in NPD + ticket for device-plugin path fallback
- lee: add canary gating for future device-plugin/operator upgrades

jin (platform): created PR #4522 to pin device-plugin; rolling back to canary nodes first. will notify when CI completes :+1:
kai (oncall): cordoned 6 nodes in us-west-2-a and tainted with `gpu-recover=true:NoSchedule`. running fix script via fleet-ssh now
maya (infra): patch script snippet for ops playbook (will add to runbook):
```
#!/bin/bash
set -e
NODE=$1
ssh $NODE "sudo ln -sfn /usr/lib/nvidia-525 /usr/lib/nvidia && sudo systemctl restart nvidia-modprobe || true"
kubectl -n gpu-operator delete pod -l name=nvidia-device-plugin --field-selector spec.nodeName=$NODE
# wait for device-plugin to register
sleep 8
kubectl get node $NODE -o jsonpath='{.status.allocatable}'
```
samir (sre): please capture logs and annotate nodes in incident ticket. we'll run a small canary for 2 hours and then uncordon if stable
lee (eng-infra): follow-ups: update our upgrade playbook to include driver symlink check, add an automated test in CI that simulates kernel path rename and ensures device-plugin handles it
maya (infra): thanks all. marking incident as active and noting severity: sev3 (partial capacity loss). will update post-mortem template after stabilization
jin (platform): also file an upstream bug for gpu-operator/device-plugin re: hardcoded path + add detect for `libcuda.so` in LD_LIBRARY_PATH
kai (oncall): all done on the immediate steps, leaving cordon in place until we get canary green. ping me for uncordon
lee (eng-infra): good catch — we avoided a large cross-region failover. thanks team :rocket:
maya (infra): closing thread for now, will add postmortem link once written
